# KTOS sovereign-prod deployment profile (Profile B).
# Ported from Adinkhepra-ASAF@28b332f docker-compose.asaf.yml; Supabase build args
# converted from hardcoded values to required env vars. See
# docs/architecture/ARCH-010-convergence-and-public-split.md for profile ownership.
#
# ASAF Sovereign Stack — Docker Compose
#
# Four containerised services:
#   asaf-api    — Go REST API (compliance graph, DAG viewer, KASA, Sekhem)
#   asaf-ui     — Next.js Compliance Graph UI
#   ollama      — Sovereign LLM (llama3.1:8b, air-gap safe)
#   khepra-mcp  — Sovereign MCP server (routes 72 tools to asaf-api, zero egress)
#
# The asaf-daemon does NOT run here.
# It runs as a systemd service on the bare metal host with:
#   sudo ASAF_MIRROR_IMAGE=asaf-mirror-rhel9:local \
#     ./bin/asaf-daemon --socket /var/run/asaf/asaf.sock --dag-path ... --key-path ...
# ASAF_MIRROR_IMAGE belongs in that systemd unit's Environment=, not in this
# compose file — it was previously (wrongly) set on asaf-api below, which
# never reads it; only asaf-daemon's staging.go does. No systemd unit file
# exists yet (deployment-packaging gap — see project_product_a_architecture
# memory, same family of gap as "no real installer bundle").
#
# The Unix socket is shared via a host-mounted volume (/var/run/asaf).
# The API container communicates with the daemon through that socket.
#
# Usage:
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.asaf.yml up -d
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.asaf.yml logs -f asaf-api
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.asaf.yml down
#
# IDE integration (Claude Code / Cursor / Antigravity — stdio):
#   { "mcpServers": { "asaf": { "command": "docker", "args": ["exec","-i","asaf-mcp","khepra-mcp"] } } }
# CI/CD / HTTP/SSE:
#   http://localhost:8765/mcp/v1
#
# Quick start (see Makefile):
#   make dev

name: asaf-sovereign

services:

  # ─── ASAF REST API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Go binary serving the compliance graph API and DAG viewer.
  # Communicates with asaf-daemon through the Unix socket on the host.
  asaf-api:
    # CONSUMED AS A PINNED IMAGE, NOT BUILT HERE (ARCH-014 §3).
    # This service previously carried `build: {context: ., dockerfile:
    # Dockerfile.adinkhepra}` — a Dockerfile that lives in Adinkhepra-ASAF and has
    # never existed in this repo, so `docker compose build` could not have worked.
    # Its image is produced by its own repo's release workflow and consumed here.
    # Build it there; pin the digest here.
    #
    # The image's ENTRYPOINT/CMD already default to "adinkhepra serve -port 8443",
    # so no command override is needed.
    image: ${ASAF_API_IMAGE:?set ASAF_API_IMAGE to a released digest, e.g. ghcr.io/nouchix/adinkhepra@sha256:...}
    container_name: asaf-api
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "8443:8443"
    volumes:
      # Share Unix socket with daemon on the host
      - /var/run/asaf:/var/run/asaf
      # Persistent DAG storage
      - asaf-dag:/var/lib/asaf/dag
      # License key (read-only)
      - ./license.adinkhepra:/etc/asaf/license.adinkhepra:ro
    environment:
      - KHEPRA_MODE=sovereign
      - KHEPRA_LLM_PROVIDER=sovereign
      - OLLAMA_HOST=http://ollama:11434
      - ASAF_DAEMON_SOCKET=/var/run/asaf/asaf.sock
      # KHEPRA_DAG_PATH (not ASAF_DAG_PATH) is what pkg/dag/factory.go actually
      # reads — see pkg/dag/global.go:31. Without this exact name the DAG falls
      # back to ~/.khepra/dag/ inside the container (lost on recreate).
      - KHEPRA_DAG_PATH=/var/lib/asaf/dag
      - KHEPRA_LICENSE_PATH=/etc/asaf/license.adinkhepra
    depends_on:
      ollama:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - asaf-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:8443/status"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ─── COMPLIANCE GRAPH UI ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Next.js frontend — Compliance Graph, Policy Editor, Staging Gate, Evidence Export
  asaf-ui:
    # CONSUMED AS A PINNED IMAGE, NOT BUILT HERE (ARCH-014 §3). Same reason as
    # asaf-api: Dockerfile.dashboard lives in Adinkhepra-ASAF.
    #
    # CARRIED-OVER CONSTRAINT, NOT RESOLVED BY THIS CHANGE: the Next.js UI needs
    # NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL / _ANON_KEY at BUILD time, because /AuthCallback
    # initializes the Supabase client at module scope. Those are build args in the
    # UI's own repo, which means the sovereign on-prem image is still built against
    # a cloud Supabase project — the "sovereign mode still depends on cloud
    # Supabase" gap flagged 2026-06-30. Moving the build out of this file does not
    # fix that; it relocates it to where the build actually happens. Tracked as an
    # open sovereignty gap in ARCH-014 §7.
    image: ${ASAF_UI_IMAGE:?set ASAF_UI_IMAGE to a released digest, e.g. ghcr.io/nouchix/adinkhepra-ui@sha256:...}
    container_name: asaf-ui
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8443
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_KHEPRA_MODE=sovereign
      - NODE_ENV=production
    depends_on:
      asaf-api:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - asaf-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:3000"]
      interval: 20s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

  # ─── SOVEREIGN LLM (Ollama) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Local AI inference — no egress, no API keys, no token costs.
  #
  # Models are NOT pulled on first start any more: asaf-network is now
  # `internal: true`, so this container cannot reach a model registry, which is
  # the entire point of an air-gapped deployment. Seed the ollama-models volume
  # first, on a connected host:
  #
  #   docker compose --profile bootstrap run --rm ollama-bootstrap
  #
  # then bring the stack up normally. `docker exec asaf-ollama ollama pull ...`
  # will fail by design once the stack is running.
  ollama:
    # Third-party image — pin the digest. An air-gapped site mirrors this into its
    # own registry, so the variable also serves as the mirror indirection point.
    image: ${OLLAMA_IMAGE:?set OLLAMA_IMAGE to a pinned digest, e.g. ollama/ollama@sha256:...}
    container_name: asaf-ollama
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"
    volumes:
      - ollama-models:/root/.ollama
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=24h
      - OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=2
    networks:
      - asaf-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "ollama", "list"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: all
              capabilities: [gpu]
        # Remove 'deploy' block entirely if no GPU available

  # ─── MODEL BOOTSTRAP (connected host only) ──────────────────────────────────
  # One-shot job that fills the ollama-models volume. It is the ONLY service
  # attached to bootstrap-egress, and it is behind a profile so it never starts
  # with the stack — `docker compose up` will not run it.
  #
  # Run this once on a host with internet access:
  #   docker compose --profile bootstrap run --rm ollama-bootstrap
  #
  # Then the volume can be exported and carried to the air-gapped host, or the
  # stack brought up in place. Steady-state operation never needs egress again.
  #
  # Override the model set with OLLAMA_BOOTSTRAP_MODELS="llama3.1:8b mistral:7b".
  ollama-bootstrap:
    profiles: ["bootstrap"]
    image: ${OLLAMA_IMAGE:?set OLLAMA_IMAGE to a pinned digest, e.g. ollama/ollama@sha256:...}
    container_name: asaf-ollama-bootstrap
    volumes:
      - ollama-models:/root/.ollama
    networks:
      - bootstrap-egress
    environment:
      # Passed through so the override below is actually reachable inside the
      # container; without this the command would always take its default.
      - OLLAMA_BOOTSTRAP_MODELS=${OLLAMA_BOOTSTRAP_MODELS:-llama3.1:8b}
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
    command:
      - |
        set -e
        ollama serve &
        server_pid=$$!
        # Wait for the local API rather than sleeping a fixed interval.
        for _ in $$(seq 1 30); do
          if ollama list >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
          sleep 1
        done
        for model in $${OLLAMA_BOOTSTRAP_MODELS:-llama3.1:8b}; do
          echo "pulling $$model"
          ollama pull "$$model"
        done
        kill $$server_pid
        wait $$server_pid 2>/dev/null || true
        echo "bootstrap complete — ollama-models volume is seeded"

  # ─── SOVEREIGN MCP SERVER ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PQC-Khepra-MCP in KHEPRA_MODE=sovereign.
  # Routes ALL 72 MCP tool calls to asaf-api on the internal network.
  # Zero external API calls — fully air-gap compatible.
  # No egress network attached — only asaf-network (internal).
  #
  # Exposes two transports:
  #   stdio  — for IDE integration (Claude Code / Cursor / Antigravity)
  #            Configure your IDE to run: docker exec -i asaf-mcp khepra-mcp
  #   HTTP/SSE (localhost:8765) — for CI/CD pipelines and web-based agents
  #
  # Claude Code config example (~/.claude/claude_desktop_config.json):
  #   {
  #     "mcpServers": {
  #       "asaf": {
  #         "command": "docker",
  #         "args": ["exec", "-i", "asaf-mcp"...
